name: Macintosh IIci ROM 368CADFE - PiStorm/Emu68 patches
notes: the four dbf loops at 0x40800880/88E/8A4/8BC count down d0.w from 0xFFFF until VIA1
timer 2 interrupts (vector $64 -> 0x40800866 -> jmp (a2)) or d0.w wraps to -1 after
65536 iterations (dbf falls through -> jmp (a2)).  The shared continuation at
0x4080084E does not.w d0, which turns the fall-through value 0xFFFF into 0, i.e. a
very fast CPU stores TimeDBRA = 0 and every derived delay collapses.  Fix: a2 points
to a 10-byte stub in the 14 bytes of zero padding after the last loop (0x408008D2,
nothing references it; the next routine 0x408008E0 is reached by braw from 0x408000B4)
that performs not.w d0 and turns a zero result into 0xFFFF (saturate), then branches
to 0x40800850 (the store).  Normal (slow-CPU) results are unchanged.

Second stub (16 Nov, later): the Pi supplies the calibration results. At JIT speed the CPU loop (TimeDBRA) overflows and the bus loops (TimeSCSIDB/TimeVIADB/TimeSCCDB) measure the bridge latency, which can leave absurd timeout counts (a saturated TimeSCSIDB made a SCSI wait last 48 minutes). The stub looks the loop's low-memory address up in a table at the slot-9 window + 0x80 (psmb.h PSMB_OFF_CALIB: 4 x {address.w, value.w}) that the kernel fills from its own measurements, and falls back to saturation when the window is absent or the entry is 0.

patches.name: calib: point a2 (loop continuation) at the stub in the padding gap
calib: the 14-byte gap only holds a long branch to the real stub
asm: bra.l   calib_stub2     | 68020 long branch: the stub is 400 KB away

patches.name: calib: stub in the zero padding at 0x629E0: take the value from the Pi's table, else saturate
asm: not.w   %d0             | d0.w = iterations completed (0 if dbf fell through)
cmp.l   #0x50534D42,(%a1) | 'PSMB': is the Pi's window there?
cmpa.w  (%a4),%a0       | (a4) = this loop's low-memory address (TimeDBRA, TimeSCCDB, TimeSCSIDB, TimeVIADB)
3:      jmp calib_store:l     | -> 0x40800850: move.w d0 to the low-memory global
